quotes.note: Jesus narrates his own experience as “I” outside dialogue, exposing the participating base narrator.
The second-person references occur within a character’s direct speech to Jesus and do not identify the narrator.
This is authorial paratext in Anne Rice’s voice, not the novel’s base narration.
Sustained first-person narration and reflection present Jesus as the participating narrator.
The clipped passage does not preserve enough context to distinguish speech from base narration.

search_log: Searched “Christ the Lord: Out of Egypt Anne Rice excerpt first chapter” and opened the authorized Bookreporter excerpt.
Searched “Christ the Lord: Out of Egypt first person narrator” and opened explicit descriptions from Publishers Weekly and the Christian Research Institute.
Searched for an Anne Rice interview about the narrator and opened Penguin Random House’s author interview, where Rice directly identifies Jesus as the first-person narrator.
Opened corroborating whole-book discussions from CBS News and Salon; both describe the novel as written in Jesus’s first-person voice.
Searched specifically for alternating narrators, multiple narrators, frame narration, and epistolary structure; found no credible evidence of another sustained narrative person.
An Anne Rice official-site result described the book as told in Jesus’s voice, but one attempted page open returned an internal error, so it was not relied upon.
person_note: The controlling narrator is Jesus, recounting his own childhood in the first person. Both event quotes independently expose that base voice, while the dialogue and authorial paratext are non-base material and the clipped final quote remains locally unresolved. An official publisher interview establishes the whole-book structure, and the authorized opening plus multiple credible reviews corroborate it. No evidence of sustained third-person, second-person, framed, or alternating narration was found; the only remaining uncertainty concerns the local attribution of q01168, not the book-level person.
